gp.text: Revenue and Gross Profit. Revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026, was $200,000, all from our related-party services agreement with Eva Defense Inc. and Eva Live Inc., under which performance commenced on August 5, 2026. We had no revenue in the three months ended September 30, 2025. Cost of revenue was $160,000, consisting of fees under our related-party subcontract with Ascendant AI LLC, which performs the services. Gross profit was $40,000, or 20% of revenue, reflecting the fixed $100,000 monthly fee under the Eva agreement and the fixed $80,000 monthly subcontract fee.

opex.text: Operating Expenses. Operating expenses for the three months ended September 30, 2026, were $520,261, consisting entirely of general and administrative expenses, compared to $507,960 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $12,301, or 2.4%. General and administrative expenses for the 2026 period comprised $416,667 of licensing-fee amortization relating to the prepaid T Stamp Inc. license, $102,225 of legal and professional fees, $723 of rent, and $646 of other expenses. The increase over the prior-year period was principally attributable to a $12,225 increase in legal and professional fees.

rd.text: Since inception, we have focused on research and development, technology acquisition, prototype development, and capital formation. During the three months ended September 30, 2026, we recognized our first revenue from contracts with customers, $200,000, under our services agreement with Eva Defense Inc. and Eva Live Inc., which are related parties, as described in Notes 7 and 8 to the accompanying unaudited consolidated financial statements. We did not generate revenue during the three or nine months ended September 30, 2025.

General and administrative expenses for the 2026 period comprised $416,667 of licensing-fee amortization relating to the prepaid T Stamp Inc. license, $102,225 of legal and professional fees, $723 of rent, and $646 of other expenses. The increase over the prior-year period was principally attributable to a $12,225 increase in legal and professional fees.

nonop.text: Other Income. Other income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was $1,000,000, consisting of an unrealized gain on our investment in Nuvora Energy, Inc. We remeasured the investment under the ASC 321 measurement alternative to $3.00 per share, the price at which Nuvora issued common stock to investors in May and June 2026 (see Note 6). The gain was recognized in the three months ended June 30, 2026, through the restatement of our previously issued financial statements for that quarter (see Note 2); accordingly, no other income was recognized in the three months ended September 30, 2026. The gain is unrealized and non-cash: it does not provide cash to fund our operations and would be realized only on a sale of the shares, for which there is no public market. There was no other income in the three or nine months ended September 30, 2025.

net.text: Net Loss. Net loss for the three months ended September 30, 2026, was $480,261, or $(0.01) per share (basic and diluted), based on 65,056,977 weighted average shares outstanding. This compares to a net loss of $507,960, or $(0.01) per share (basic and diluted), based on 66,056,977 weighted average shares outstanding, for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The $27,699 decrease in net loss reflects $40,000 of gross profit from our first revenue-generating contract, partially offset by the $12,301 increase in general and administrative expenses. No other income or expense was recognized in the three months ended September 30, 2026; the $1,000,000 unrealized gain on our investment in Nuvora Energy, Inc. was recognized in the three months ended June 30, 2026, as restated (see Note 2).

ocf.text: Operating Activities. Net cash used in operating activities was $42,565 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $43,678 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. In each period, the net loss was substantially offset by non-cash amortization of prepaid licensing of $1,250,001 and by increases in related-party accounts payable and accrued expenses. In the 2026 period, the net loss also included the $1,000,000 non-cash unrealized gain on investment, which is deducted in arriving at net cash used in operating activities, and $100,000 of the $200,000 billed under the Eva Defense agreement remained uncollected at September 30, 2026.

wc.text: Since inception, we have funded our operations primarily through equity financing and short-term working-capital advances from a related party and, beginning in the third quarter of 2026, through collections under our services agreement with Eva Defense Inc. and Eva Live Inc. As of September 30, 2026, we had cash of $6,119, compared to $16,084 as of December 31, 2025. Our principal uses of cash are payments to related-party service providers, WaveDrone development costs, and legal and professional fees.

profile.name: Boumarang Inc.
profile.industry: Search, Detection, Navigation, Guidance, Aeronautical Sys
profile.category: Non-accelerated filer · Smaller reporting company · Emerging growth company

intro.text: The Company (“us,” “we,” and “our”) was incorporated on July 26, 2024 (“Inception”), as Boumarang Inc. (“Boumarang”) under the laws of the State of Delaware. The Company is based in Irvine, California, with an additional location in Austin, Texas. The Company aims to revolutionize industry operations with sustainable, long-range, intelligent drones. In October 2024, the Company established Boumarang Pty Ltd. in Australia, through which it conducts its business with the Australian government and the non-government sector. At present, there are no significant operations of Boumarang Pty Ltd. Boumarang aims to revolutionize industrial operations with sustainable, long-range drones powered by hydrogen fuel cells, targeting sectors like natural resource monitoring, infrastructure analysis, agriculture, and forestry.

s.t: The Company remeasured its investment in Nuvora Energy, Inc. to its fair value of $ 3,000,000 ($ 3.00 per share) on the basis of observable transaction prices in May and June 2026, a Level 2 input, as described in Note 6, and recognized the remeasurement in the three months ended June 30, 2026, as restated (see Note 2, “Restatement of Previously Issued Financial Statements”).

On October 27, 2025, the Company became the beneficial owner of 1,000,000 shares of common stock of Nuvora Energy, Inc. (“Nuvora”), a privately held Delaware corporation, recorded as an Investment in private equity securities at an initial carrying amount of $ 2,000,000 ($ 2.00 per share).
The unrealized gain on the Company’s investment in Nuvora is not subject to federal or state income tax until realized, and accordingly no current income tax was recognized.

No other income or expense was recognized in the three months ended September 30, 2026; the $1,000,000 unrealized gain on our investment in Nuvora Energy, Inc. was recognized in the three months ended June 30, 2026, as restated (see Note 2).

Other income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was $1,000,000, consisting of an unrealized gain on our investment in Nuvora Energy, Inc. We remeasured the investment under the ASC 321 measurement alternative to $3.00 per share, the price at which Nuvora issued common stock to investors in May and June 2026 (see Note 6).

The Company has restated its previously issued unaudited consolidated financial statements as of and for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, by filing Amendment No. 1 on Form 10-Q/A to its Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for that period, to correct an error in the measurement of its investment in Nuvora Energy, Inc. (“Nuvora”) described in Note 6.

During the three months ended June 30, 2026 (as restated), the Company remeasured its investment in Nuvora to $ 3,000,000 on the basis of Nuvora’s issuance of common stock to investors at $ 3.00 per share in May and June 2026, and recognized the remeasurement through the restatement of its previously issued financial statements for that period (see Note 2).
Our investment in private equity securities consists of 1,000,000 common shares of Nuvora Energy, Inc. carried at $3,000,000.
